JurassiCraft is a mod made to bring prehistoric creatures to the world of Minecraft. It is inspired by Jurassic Park, but is not limited to all JP canon: as many creatures and features as possible will be added! Creatures are made Jurassic Park style, by obtaining fossils or amber, using the fossils or amber to create DNA, inserting the DNA into eggs, and hatching the eggs. The mod recently merged with two other mods, entitled the Bygone Age Mod and the Fossil Hunting Mod, which will bring users a more complete modded-Minecraft experience.

Alright, off of the top of my head...

  • More JavaScript - This is one of the more practical concerns. There are a lot of people out there that like to minimize JavaScript use as much as possible because it's yet another thing to be exploited. "Oh, that's silly! EVERYONE uses JavaScript!" some might counter. And yes, that's true. And because of it all of its ugly flaws smack you in the face like a wet tuna, so they don't like more of it. As they say, "if it ain't broke, don't fix it," and clicking for additional pages is a good way to do that. "But Reddit does it, and clicking is just more JavaScript!" Others might proclaim. And yes, that's true, but it's a) activated on demand, which is a lot less aggregious, and b) it's still not all that good. Perhaps I left my sensibilities back in 1998, but I still prefer avoiding JavaScript where not necessary for a multitude of reasons, including efficiency and security.

  • Frustration - This is psychological. When I reach the end of a page, I want it to be the end of the page unless I see otherwise. This has a slightly practical element as well. I drop down to the bottom of the page and don't want that to automatically assume I want more - because often I don't. "I'll just scroll down to the bottom of the pae, THEN I'll get to actual work -- AAGGGGHHHH!" Frustrating. Also, pressing the "end" key doesn't mean you'll get the actual "end" of what you've loaded so far - it just means you'll get what is effectively NEAR the end. Not always what I wanted.

  • Printing - This is related to the last concern in frustration. It's difficult to use the printing function with this, especially if you want to see all the content you're asking to be printed WITHOUT loading up new stuff by mistake. While you can use Print Preview, not only is this more combersome, it's also not the most helpful; while modern web browsers have improved this to some extent, I still find that printing with web pages can be very difficult if you're looking for something specific, and sometimes you can't even find an acceptable compromise without dragging it out of the browser and editing. Adding in more problems to this process is not helpful, especially since some of these people have eyesight problems and may want to read paper when their eyes get too tired to directly use the Internet.

  • The UX People - This is where I get a bit opinionated and, I suppose, slightly philosophical. There has been a lot of work at "modernizing" the user interface that results in some rather absurd assumptions. For instance, lobotomizing Gnome iteratively (there's a reason Ubuntu isn't doing so well lately, and it isn't just the spyware crap), as well as removing arrows from scrollbars, and ultimately the agony over Windows 8 which also screams at an inevitable march away from standard computers and towards tablets. This is part and parcel to that - unnecessary and an attempt to dictate at the user what the computer will do for them rather than ask them what they want, or let the user directly specify it, even if they end up clipping off otherwise valuable functions, and giving no alternative to this choice.

  • Bandwidth concerns - This one isn't so much of a concern on Voat as it is elsewhere on the Internet, but it's rather ironic given the last point touched on tablet users and their needs. Automatically loading things means that users of tablets, cell phones, and other limited-bandwidth Internet connections may well be faced with a choice - leave some already-loaded content to rot, because they're low on bandwidth, or keep scrolling down to see everything they've loaded and wasting more bandwidth.

So this is why I don't like it, and I'm sure there are many more reasons, since I'm trying to put my thoughts on this together logically. Now I'm not knocking people who do like it; if they do, so much the better. I'm not even knocking the feature, because I can see it being useful, and there have been a few cases where it was indeed useful for me. The thing is, though, that in my experience, most websites that implement this implement only this, except for a few where you go through some considerable gymnastics to trick it into thinking you're using an older/lobotomized web browser. They assume it's an upgrade for everyone. It isn't. For some of us, it's a downgrade, and we're left with no options to change it. Considering the attempts to bash everything on the Internet into something tablet friendly, even if it was grossly inappropriate, this is just another frustration along these lines for many people who find these attempts backwards and frustrating. As such, I'm fine with the feature, so long as there's an option to turn it on or off. I was not bashing your extension, which I'm sure that many people find useful. I was trying to get something preemptive in there in case someone got the bright idea to start a messaging campaign to try to get this turned on for everyone because OBVIOUSLY (to them) it's an upgrade in all cases for all users. It isn't.

(Incidentally, if whoever is responsible for removing arrows from scrollbars without a way to turn them back on is out there? I'm normally not this rude, but from the bottom of my heart: Fuck you, you son of a bitch. Also, look at the flames Google got when they tried to pull this shit with Chrome - and they deserved it, too.)
